pages.title: Stars in the Sky
pages.content:
It is a quiet summer night. Yusuf and his dad are camping. They have got a small tent. Next to the tent, there is a big blanket on the grass. They sit on the blanket.

There are many stars in the sky. “Dad, look! That star is very bright,” Yusuf says. Dad smiles. “There is a story about a young man. He looks at the stars, too. His name is Abraham. Do you want to hear his story?” he asks. “Yes, please!” Yusuf says.

“Abraham lives in Babylon,” Dad says. “And young Abraham has got a big question in his heart: ‘Who makes the sky and the stars?’”

“One night, Abraham sees a bright star. Then the star goes away. He sees the moon. The moon goes away. In the morning, he sees the sun. In the evening, the sun goes away, too. Abraham knows: Allah makes the star, the moon, and the sun. Allah never goes away! Then Allah chooses Abraham to be His Messenger.”

pages.title: Stones in a Big House
pages.content:
Yusuf thinks. “Dad, do the people of Babylon know Allah?” he asks.

“No, Yusuf,” Dad says. “They have got many idols. Idols are big stones. They are in a big house. The people pray to them. But idols can’t see. They can’t hear. They can’t talk. Abraham’s father makes idols, too. Abraham is sad. Abraham wants to tell them about Allah. Abraham has got a plan.”

vocabulary.definition: Things of stone or wood. Some people pray to them.
Talk to Allah (or a god) and ask for help.
An idea: what to do and how.

pages.title: Abraham’s Plan
pages.content:
“What is his plan, Dad?” Yusuf asks. His eyes are big.

“One day, all the people go out of the city,” Dad says. “Abraham goes to the big house. He breaks the idols. He only leaves the biggest idol. In the evening, the people come back. They see the idols on the floor. They are very angry! They ask Abraham about the idols. Abraham says, ‘Ask the big idol. Can it talk?’ The people are quiet. Stones can’t talk!”

pages.title: The Fire
pages.content:
Yusuf laughs. “Stones can’t talk!” he says. “Are the people sorry now?”

“No, Yusuf,” Dad says. “They are very angry. They make a very big fire. They put Abraham in the fire. But Abraham is not afraid. Allah is with him. Allah says, ‘O fire, be cold and safe for Abraham.’ The fire is not hot now. Abraham comes out. He is fine!”

Yusuf opens his eyes wide. “Allah is great!” he says.

“Yes,” Dad says. “Then Abraham leaves Babylon. He goes to new places.”

vocabulary.definition: Something very hot, red and yellow.
Not in danger; OK.
Goes out of a place.

pages.title: Water in the Desert
pages.content:
“Where does Abraham go, Dad?” Yusuf asks.

“He goes very far,” Dad says. “Years later, he has got a wife, Hagar, and a baby son, Ishmael. They come to a quiet place in the desert. There are two small hills there, Safa and Marwah. There is no water. There are no people. Hagar and Ishmael stay near the hills. Allah has got a plan. He tells Abraham to go back. So Abraham goes. On the way, he prays for his family: ‘O Allah, please take care of my family.’ Allah is with them.

“Soon, baby Ishmael is very thirsty. Hagar wants to find water. She runs between the two hills seven times. Then water comes out under Ishmael’s feet. It is Zamzam!”

Yusuf smiles. “We have got Zamzam water at home, Dad!” he says.

vocabulary.definition: A very hot, dry place with sand.
You want to drink water.

pages.title: The House of Allah
pages.content:
“Yes, we have,” Dad says. “People come to the water. They live there. It is a city now. Its name is Mecca. Years later, Ishmael is a young man, and Abraham is with his family again. Allah gives Abraham and Ishmael a very special job. They build the Ka’ba together. Ishmael brings stones. Abraham puts them on the walls. They pray to Allah. The Ka’ba is the House of Allah.”

Yusuf looks at the stars again. “I want to see the Ka’ba one day, Dad,” he says.

“In sha Allah, Yusuf,” Dad says. He holds Yusuf’s hand. “It is time for bed. Look! The stars say goodnight to us!”

vocabulary.definition: Make a house or a wall.
